issues.legal_issue: A usufructuary mortgagee entitled to possess the premises and receive their rent is a landlord within the rent-control statute’s definition.
material_facts: The owner granted the respondents a usufructuary mortgage over the premises occupied by a tenant.
The mortgage entitled the respondents to possession and to receive the property’s rents and profits on their own account.
The respondents sought eviction of the tenant under the rent-control statute.
issues.conclusion: A usufructuary mortgagee with possession is a landlord within the statutory definition because the mortgagee is entitled to receive rent on their own account.
issues.legal_principle: Section 3(h) of the Karnataka Rent Control Act, 1961 defines landlord inclusively to cover a person receiving or entitled to receive rent. Under Section 58(d) of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, a usufructuary mortgagee is entitled to possession or to receive rents and profits and apply them to interest or the mortgage money. The Court’s conclusion accords with V. Baluswamy Servai v. N. Raju Servai, T. Ezhumalai v. Padmavathi Ammal, Aswatharamiah v. Special Deputy Commissioner, and the Full Bench ruling in R. Vijendra v. H.R. & A.C.

rule.if: rent_control_eviction_case and usufructuary_mortgage and entitled_to_possession and entitled_to_rent_on_own_account

predicates.rent_control_eviction_case: A person seeks to evict a tenant in a proceeding under rent-control law.
predicates.usufructuary_mortgage: The property owner has granted a mortgage under which the mortgagee receives the property’s usufruct.
predicates.entitled_to_possession: The mortgagee is entitled to possess the mortgaged property.
predicates.entitled_to_rent_on_own_account: The mortgagee is entitled to receive the premises’ rent on the mortgagee’s own account.

issues.definition: When a rent-control eviction case involves a usufructuary mortgagee entitled to possession and to receive rent on their own account, the mortgagee is a landlord.

issues.legal_issue: A usufructuary mortgagee with possession may seek eviction of a tenant for the mortgagee’s own reasonable and bona fide need to occupy the premises.
material_facts: The respondents held a usufructuary mortgage over the tenanted premises and were entitled to possession.
They sought eviction to use the premises for their business, having been displaced from another rented business premises.
The courts below found that their need was bona fide, and that finding was not challenged in the appeal.
issues.conclusion: A mortgagee with possession stands on a par with the owner for this purpose and may seek recovery of the premises for the mortgagee’s own bona fide requirement, subject to the statutory conditions for eviction.
issues.legal_principle: Section 21(1)(h) of the Karnataka Rent Control Act, 1961 allows eviction where premises are reasonably and bona fide required by the landlord for occupation. Its explanation excludes a Collector or Estate Manager but does not exclude a mortgagee with possession. Section 76(a) of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 requires a mortgagee in possession to manage the property as a person of ordinary prudence would manage their own property. The Court relied on Mathur Lal v. Keshar Bai and approved the views in V. Baluswamy Servai v. N. Raju Servai and R. Vijendra v. H.R. & A.C. Section 21(4) separately protects a tenant where eviction would cause the tenant greater hardship than refusal would cause the landlord.

rule.if: rent_control_eviction_case and usufructuary_mortgage and entitled_to_possession and bona_fide_own_occupation_need

predicates.rent_control_eviction_case: A person seeks to evict a tenant in a proceeding under rent-control law.
predicates.usufructuary_mortgage: The property owner has granted a mortgage under which the mortgagee receives the property’s usufruct.
predicates.entitled_to_possession: The mortgagee is entitled to possess the mortgaged property.
predicates.bona_fide_own_occupation_need: The mortgagee reasonably and genuinely needs the premises for the mortgagee’s own occupation.

issues.definition: A mortgagee entitled to possession under a usufructuary mortgage may seek eviction for the mortgagee’s own reasonable and genuine occupation need in a rent-control eviction case.

issues.legal_issue: The possibility that an owner might use a sham usufructuary mortgage to procure a tenant’s eviction does not, by itself, bar a mortgagee with possession from seeking eviction for bona fide need.
material_facts: The tenant alleged that the mortgage was a sham created to enable eviction after the tenant refused to pay higher rent.
The trial court rejected the sham-transaction defence, and the appeal did not challenge the finding that the mortgage had been obtained.
The courts found the mortgagees’ need bona fide.
The Court noted that the mortgagee had to prove reasonable and bona fide need and that the comparative-hardship restriction applied to an eviction order.
issues.conclusion: The hypothetical risk of a sham mortgage did not justify denying a mortgagee with possession the right to seek eviction; eviction would still require proof of bona fide need and compliance with the comparative-hardship protection.
issues.legal_principle: Section 21(1)(h) of the Karnataka Rent Control Act, 1961 requires reasonable and bona fide need, and Section 21(4) bars eviction where the tenant would suffer greater hardship than the landlord would suffer if eviction were refused. Those safeguards address the concern that an owner might use a mortgagee to obtain eviction improperly.

rule.if: rent_control_eviction_case and mortgage_transaction_established and bona_fide_need_proved and comparative_hardship_test_applies

predicates.rent_control_eviction_case: A person seeks to evict a tenant in a proceeding under rent-control law.
predicates.mortgage_transaction_established: The evidence establishes that the owner granted a mortgage over the premises to the mortgagee.
predicates.bona_fide_need_proved: The mortgagee proves a reasonable and genuine need to occupy the premises.
predicates.comparative_hardship_test_applies: The proceeding requires the court to consider whether eviction would cause the tenant greater hardship than refusal would cause the landlord.

issues.definition: Where a mortgage transaction is established, bona fide need is proved, and comparative hardship must be considered, the possibility of sham transactions alone does not bar the mortgagee’s eviction claim.
